item.description: Kiteworks, the secure file-sharing and managed file-transfer vendor formerly known as Accellion, asked customers on 25 September to shut their systems down for a weekend window after receiving threat intelligence from federal intelligence authorities. In a 27 September release it said hosted systems had been restored and a fix deployed for a flaw in its Advanced Forms feature, which it says fewer than 1% of customers use. Kiteworks reports no indication the flaw was ever exploited, and it has lifted the shutdown advisory. No CVE has been published for that flaw, and the agency has not been named. Separately, on 1 October Kiteworks published fixes for 126 vulnerabilities, 11 of them critical. The worst, CVE-2026-54154, is an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in Kiteworks Email Protection Gateway before 9.4.1, reported through YesWeHack and not exploited. Kiteworks has not said whether CVE-2026-54154 is the flaw behind the shutdown, so this card does not link them. The card is downgraded from High because the feared attack has not materialised. - Kiteworks press releases and advisories; BleepingComputer; The Record - Shutdown advisory 25 Sep 2026; restore and fix 27 Sep 2026; advisory batch 1 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] MikroTik RouterOS: CVE-2026-67279 joined KEV on 25 September and, paired with CVE-2026-86060, gives an unauthenticated attacker full control of an exposed router — a separate web-management flaw, CVE-2026-84411, followed in a CISA advisory on 29 September
item.description: CISA added CVE-2026-67279 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 25 September with a federal deadline of 28 September. The KEV entry says the SSH flaw “could allow an unauthenticated client to open a session channel and send an exec request” and “can be chained to achieve unauthenticated exploitation of CVE-2026-86060”, a RouterOS argument-injection flaw. It is rated CVSS 6.9 (version not stated), a score that undersells the chain. CVE-2026-86060 and CVE-2026-67277 were added to KEV on 10 September. CERT Polska reported on 5 September that a two-flaw SSH chain it calls “MikroTrick” had been exploited in the wild since about 2 September. Its 22 September technical analysis names the chain: CVE-2026-67279 combined with CVE-2026-86060, which gives full administrative control without a password, SSH key or completed authentication. Fixed builds are RouterOS 7.24.2, 7.23.4 and 6.49.21; the related CVE-2026-67278 needs 7.24.3 or 7.23.6 because the earlier fix was incomplete. Shadowserver counted more than 122,500 MikroTik devices with SSH reachable from the internet in early September. That is an exposure count, not a count of unpatched or compromised routers. CVE-2026-67276 is not in KEV. MikroTik routers are common at branch offices, small ISPs and remote sites. Update, 29 September: CISA advisory ICSA-26-272-06 covers a separate flaw, CVE-2026-84411, a pre-authentication integer underflow in the RouterOS web-management interface that can give remote code execution or denial of service. It is rated CVSS v3.1 9.8 / v4 9.3 and fixed in RouterOS 7.24. It is not in KEV, and no exploitation has been reported to CISA. - CISA KEV catalog; CISA ICS advisory ICSA-26-272-06; CERT Polska (incl. its 22 Sep technical analysis); The Hacker News; BleepingComputer - CERT Polska 5 Sep 2026; KEV additions 10 Sep 2026 and 25 Sep 2026; CISA advisory 29 Sep 2026

item.title: [Medium] Attackers are probing Rejetto HFS servers for CVE-2026-61500, a flaw found with an AI model that lets them forge an admin session and run code — fixed since July
item.category: Advisory — Exploitation reported, not in KEV
item.description: VulnCheck has reported exploitation activity against CVE-2026-61500 in the Rejetto HTTP File Server (HFS), described as small-scale reconnaissance from a China Telecom address against targets in Japan and the United States. A weak random-number generator used to sign session cookies lets an attacker forge an administrator session and then run code through the server’s scripting feature. It is rated CVSS v4 9.3 (v3.1 9.8). HFS 3.0.0 to 3.2.0 are affected, and 3.2.1, released on 13 July, fixes it. Horizon3.ai found the flaw using an AI model. It is not in CISA’s KEV catalog. HFS is a small file server that people often run ad hoc to share files, so the risk sits in copies nobody in IT knows about. - VulnCheck via SecurityWeek; Horizon3.ai; BleepingComputer; The Hacker News - Fixed 13 Jul 2026; exploitation reported 5 Oct 2026

item.title: [Medium] Dell’s Container Storage Modules carry two CVSS 10.0 missing-authentication flaws and four more rated 9.6–9.9 — fixed in 1.18.0, with no workaround
item.description: Dell advisory DSA-2026-448, published on 2 October, fixes six critical flaws in Dell Container Storage Modules (CSM), the Kubernetes components that connect clusters to Dell storage. CVE-2026-63688 (CVSS 10.0) is missing authentication on the authorization module’s storage gRPC server, which exposes storage-backend administrator credentials. CVE-2026-63692 (10.0) is missing authentication in the authorization proxy and tenant service. CVE-2026-67269 (9.9) lets a low-privilege user reach root on cluster nodes through the custom-resource reconciler. CVE-2026-54472 (9.8) and CVE-2026-61421 (9.8) are hard-coded credentials and a hard-coded JWT signing key that allow forged administrator tokens, and CVE-2026-67273 (9.6) is a template-engine flaw that allows privilege escalation and RBAC tampering. All versions before 1.18.0 are affected, and Dell lists no workaround. No exploitation has been reported. The prize is storage credentials and root across a cluster, so these matter most where CSM runs in shared or multi-tenant clusters. - Dell DSA-2026-448; The Hacker News - Published 2 Oct 2026

item.title: [Critical] WordPress core CVE-2026-87902 is now in CISA KEV with a 28 September deadline — exploit attempts began within five hours of the fix; update to 7.1.2 even if you installed 7.1.1 earlier this month
item.description: WordPress 7.1.2, released on 22 September with backports down to the 4.7 branch, fixes CVE-2026-87902. It is an unauthenticated path traversal that allows local PHP file inclusion and remote code execution, rated CVSS 9.2, and was found by Robert Ressl. Code execution needs two conditions. The active parent or child theme must have a top-level directory whose name starts with page- (such as page-templates), and there must be a readable PHP file outside the theme directories that can be abused. The advisory notes that the official PHP Docker image and the default cPanel configuration with PHP before 8.5 meet the second condition. Patchstack recorded the first malicious requests at 17:44 UTC on 22 September, under five hours after the patch. By 23 September the traffic had increased tenfold and moved from probing with double-encoded traversal strings to writing files such as wp-pear-rce-flag.php, poc87902.php, luci_*.php and zeta_*.php into /tmp and /var/tmp. No confirmed site compromises have been counted. Update, 25 September: CISA added CVE-2026-87902 to the KEV catalog, listing it as remote file inclusion, with a federal deadline of 28 September. This is a different bug from Click2Shell, which was fixed in 7.1.1. Sites updated to 7.1.1 still need 7.1.2. - WordPress release notes; Patchstack; CISA KEV catalog; BleepingComputer; The Hacker News - Fixed 22 Sep 2026; exploitation from 22 Sep 2026; escalation reported 23 Sep 2026; KEV 25 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] CISA now says ransomware gangs are exploiting JetBrains TeamCity CVE-2026-63077 — about 160 internet-exposed servers were still unpatched two months after the fix
item.description: On 24 September CISA changed its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities entry for CVE-2026-63077 to “Known To Be Used in Ransomware Campaigns”. The flaw is in TeamCity On-Premises, JetBrains’ build server. JetBrains says it lets “an unauthenticated attacker” use the TeamCity agent polling protocol to “bypass authentication checks and execute arbitrary operating system commands.” JetBrains fixed it on 25 July. CISA added it to KEV on 5 August, and JetBrains confirmed in-the-wild exploitation on 7 August. No ransomware group has been named. Shadowserver counted about 160 unpatched TeamCity servers exposed to the internet in late September, down from about 700 after the patch. JetBrains warns that exploitation can “expose TeamCity data, configurations, and stored credentials, modify server state, and potentially compromise the integrity of build artifacts and downstream CI/CD pipelines.” A build server holds signing keys, deployment credentials and source code, so a compromise does not stay on the build server. Any server that was exposed and unpatched after late July needs a compromise check as well as the patch. - CISA KEV catalog; JetBrains; BleepingComputer; SC Media; Shadowserver - Fixed 25 Jul 2026; KEV 5 Aug 2026; ransomware flag 24 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] CISA adds Adobe Commerce/Magento CVE-2026-71362 and WSO2 API Manager CVE-2026-5430 to KEV with a 27 September deadline — one lets attackers into other shoppers’ accounts, the other accepts forged sign-in tokens
item.description: Two flaws went into the KEV catalog on 24 September, both with a federal deadline of 27 September. Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source CVE-2026-71362, CVSS 9.1, is an incorrect-authorisation flaw fixed in Adobe’s August bulletin APSB26-92. It needs no login and no user interaction. The Hacker News reports that attackers switch a customer’s session into another customer’s account and read that customer’s private data. Sansec detected and blocked exploitation attempts in August, and Previdian’s sensors saw another attempt on 10 September. Adobe has not yet confirmed exploitation in its own advisory. Affected versions are Adobe Commerce 2.4.4–2.4.9, Commerce B2B 1.3.3–1.5.3 and Magento Open Source 2.4.6–2.4.9 before the August 2026 releases. WSO2 CVE-2026-5430 affects API Manager 4.1.0–4.6.0 and the 4.5.0 and 4.6.0 releases of API Control Plane, Traffic Manager and Universal Gateway. WSO2’s advisory WSO2-2026-5328 says “JWT authentication can be bypassed when a token is signed using an unsupported algorithm, allowing unauthorized access”. It is rated CVSS 10.0 (9.8 in single-tenant deployments) and was fixed in April. watchTowr has seen forged tokens used against it since 13 September. CISA’s own KEV entry titles it a “Multiple Products Path Traversal Vulnerability”. This card uses WSO2’s own description. No attribution has been published for either flaw. - CISA KEV catalog; Adobe APSB26-92; WSO2 advisory WSO2-2026-5328; The Hacker News; Sansec; watchTowr via SecurityWeek - KEV additions 24 Sep 2026; deadline 27 Sep 2026

item.title: [High] Roundcube Webmail CVE-2026-48842 is now being exploited, Canada’s Cyber Centre says — a pre-authentication SQL injection fixed in May, with about 523,000 Roundcube instances online
item.description: The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security updated its advisory AV26-503 on 21 September to say: “Open-source reporting indicates that CVE-2026-48842 is being exploited in the wild.” It gives no detail on who is exploiting it or how widely. The flaw is an unauthenticated SQL injection in Roundcube’s built-in virtuser_query plugin, where crafted backslash sequences get past the plugin’s escaping. BleepingComputer reports that it can let an attacker bypass authentication, run database commands and steal data from the Roundcube database. SecurityWeek gives it a CVSS score of 8.1. Roundcube fixed it in 1.6.16 and 1.7.1 on 24 May. Shadowserver sees about 523,000 Roundcube instances online, patch state unknown, and exposure depends on whether virtuser_query is enabled. The flaw is not reported as KEV-listed. Roundcube is the webmail front end for many universities, hosting providers, ISPs and smaller organisations, and it often runs on a host’s shared platform that nobody inside the organisation patches. - Canadian Centre for Cyber Security AV26-503; Roundcube; BleepingComputer; SecurityWeek - Fixed 24 May 2026; exploitation reported 21 Sep 2026; covered 24–25 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] The Check Point VPN flaw the Dutch NCSC warned about is now exploited — Check Point has seen attacks on Spark firewalls since 12 September, and CISA gave federal agencies until 25 September
item.description: This card has changed state. CVE-2026-85102 is improper validation of certificate data during VPN negotiation on Check Point Security Gateways and Spark firewalls. It gives an unauthenticated attacker remote code execution. Check Point released fixes on 9 September (sk1000117). In an advisory on 22 September it said: “Starting September 12, 2026, we observed a wave of exploitation attempts against Spark customers.” Spark is the SMB line, locally or centrally managed, and Help Net Security reports the attempts came from anonymisation infrastructure and were aimed at small businesses and managed service providers. CISA added the flaw to the KEV catalog on 22 September with a federal deadline of 25 September, which has now passed. Check Point gives no customer count and no attribution. It has published usable indicators: exploit certificates with subjects CN=vpn, CN=vpn-user or CN=vpnuser, with OU=users and O=global. The companion flaw from the same NCSC warning, CVE-2026-85103, a heap overflow in the VPN certificate decoder, was not part of the 22 September KEV additions. An earlier edition said there was still a window before exploitation. That window closed on 12 September, ten days before the confirmation. The same Check Point advisory disclosed a second, separate exploited flaw in management servers, CVE-2026-93616. - Check Point advisory; CISA KEV catalog; BleepingComputer; Help Net Security; Dutch NCSC - Fixes 9 Sep 2026; exploitation from 12 Sep 2026; advisory and KEV listing 22 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] A second Check Point management-server flaw, CVE-2026-93616, was exploited as a zero-day in July — it is not the over-long-username bug, it was fixed on 22 September, and you need to hunt back two months
item.description: Check Point’s 22 September advisory disclosed CVE-2026-93616. It is a pre-authentication path traversal in the Security Management web service that lets an attacker execute scripts and load Java classes. Check Point says it saw a “handful of pinpointed attacks on July 23, 2026”, two months before the fix (sk1000171) became available on 22 September. Help Net Security lists the affected products as Security Management Server, Multi-Domain Security Management Server, Log Server, Multi-Domain Log Server and SmartEvent. CISA added it to the KEV catalog on 22 September with a federal deadline of 25 September, now passed. Neither the targets nor the actor have been named. This is a different flaw from CVE-2026-91843, the over-long-username stack overflow Check Point disclosed on 16 September, which is not in KEV. Both are on the same servers, so one change window should close both. A management server pushes policy to every gateway beneath it, and this one was exploited for two months before anyone could patch. - Check Point advisory; CISA KEV catalog; Help Net Security; The Hacker News; SecurityWeek - Exploited 23 Jul 2026; fixed, disclosed and KEV-listed 22 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] F5 BIG-IP APM has an exploited unauthenticated RCE, CVE-2026-94127 — only systems where APM acts as an OAuth authorization server are exposed, and the fixes are engineering hotfixes
item.description: F5 disclosed CVE-2026-94127 on 22 September (K000162605). It is a heap-based buffer overflow in BIG-IP Access Policy Manager, rated CVSS 9.8 (v3.1) and 9.3 (v4.0), which lets an unauthenticated attacker run code by sending crafted traffic to a virtual server. The condition is narrow. A system is exposed only when an access policy and an OAuth authorization server profile sit on the same virtual server, meaning APM is issuing OAuth tokens. Restricting the management interface does not help, because the attack arrives on the data plane, and Appliance mode systems are equally affected. F5 confirms exploitation but has not described the attacker, the victims or when it started. Rapid7 reported no confirmed public proof-of-concept as of 22 September. CISA added it to KEV on 22 September with a 25 September deadline, now passed. The fixes are engineering hotfixes for 21.1.0, 17.5.0–17.5.1 and 17.1.0–17.1.3, and F5 support can provide a temporary iRule mitigation. The OAuth configuration limits the number of exposed systems. The organisations that run APM this way are usually banks, government bodies and telecoms, where BIG-IP is the front door to single sign-on. - F5 advisory K000162605; CISA KEV catalog; Rapid7; The Hacker News; CERT-EU - Disclosed and KEV-listed 22 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator has an exploited maximum-severity flaw, CVE-2026-93952 — the SD-WAN controller that pushes configuration to every branch edge
item.description: Arista has disclosed CVE-2026-93952, an improper input validation flaw in the certificate-based authentication between VeloCloud Edges and the VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO). BleepingComputer calls it maximum severity, and Arista’s advisory 0183 rates it CVSS 10.0 (v3.1). It is low complexity and needs no privileges or user interaction. The attacker does need network access to the VCO web interface and “the public portion of the VeloCloud Edge authentication certificate”, and certificate-based Edge authentication must be enabled. Arista says the issue “was discovered externally and is known to be actively exploited”. Affected versions are VCO 6.1.3.7 and earlier and 7.0.0.2 and earlier. The fixed releases are 5.2.3.16 and 6.4.2.8 or later. Arista says hosted VCO has been updated, so this is mainly an on-premises problem. CISA added the flaw to KEV on 22 September with a 25 September deadline, now passed. Published indicators include connections from 142.93.149.77 and 104.248.126.159, an x-vc-opt HTTP header, and encoded characters or unusual paths in access logs. An orchestrator compromise matters because the orchestrator configures every edge beneath it: branch offices, shops, clinics and the managed-service customers of carriers. - Arista Security Advisory 0183; CISA KEV catalog; BleepingComputer; SecurityWeek - KEV-listed 22 Sep 2026; Arista advisory and reporting 22–23 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] Cisco ISE has a CVSS 10.0 zero-day under active exploitation — unauthenticated root on the system that decides who gets onto your network, with no workaround
item.description: Cisco has confirmed active exploitation of CVE-2026-76460, a CVSS 10.0 flaw in Identity Services Engine that it describes as insufficient authentication control on an API endpoint. An unauthenticated remote attacker can bypass the web management interface and get root command execution. ISE and ISE-PIC 3.0 through 3.5 are affected. Fixes are in 3.1 Patch 12, 3.2 P11, 3.3 P12, 3.4 P7 and 3.5 P4, and there is no workaround. CISA added the flaw to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 16 September with a three-day federal deadline of 19 September, now passed. The advisory was still at its original revision on 21 September, and Cisco has published no exposure count. No actor has been named, and Cisco warns that attackers may “remove or hide evidence of exploitation”. This is the third actively exploited ISE flaw since June 2025, after CVE-2025-20281 and CVE-2025-20337. It is also Cisco’s second exploited zero-day in a matter of days, after the Secure Email Gateway flaw below. The product’s role is why it ranks among the most urgent items on this page. ISE is the policy engine that decides which users and devices get onto the wired, wireless and VPN network, and what they can reach once there. VulnCheck notes that root on ISE lets an attacker rewrite network access policy, pull stored credentials, delete logs and move laterally. The control meant to contain an intruder ends up working for the intruder. - Cisco PSIRT; CISA KEV catalog; CyberScoop; The Hacker News; Help Net Security - Advisory and KEV listing 16 Sep 2026; reported 17 Sep 2026

item.title: [High] CISA added a Zyxel GS1900 switch flaw patched in June to KEV on 21 September — GreyNoise ties it to one actor who pulled configs and root hashes from 996 switches in 48 countries, and stole 18,566 government records through WordPress
item.description: CISA added CVE-2026-7273 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 21 September with a federal deadline of 24 September. It is a stack-based buffer overflow in the CGI program of Zyxel’s GS1900-series managed switches (GS1900-8, 8HP, 10HP, 16, 24, 24E, 24EP, 24HPv2, 48 and 48HPv2) that lets an unauthenticated attacker on the LAN side execute operating-system commands with a crafted HTTP request; Zyxel published fixed firmware, 2.90(AAHH.2)C0 and per-model equivalents, on 16 June, and its advisory gives no CVSS score. The KEV entry says “LAN-based”, so exposure runs through management-plane reachability rather than the open internet. GreyNoise’s report the same day documents what it calls the first in-the-wild exploitation: a single actor, active since 7 May and assessed as a Chinese speaker, used a PyArmor-obfuscated Python tool to exploit 996 GS1900 switches in 48 countries, led by Italy (133), the United States (129) and Taiwan (123), pulling configurations and root-level hashed credentials over TFTP; 564 of the victims still used factory-default credentials. The same actor exploited two WordPress flaws, CVE-2026-63030 and CVE-2026-60137, to steal at least 18,566 records, including accounts, plaintext passwords and personal data tied to law-enforcement and government agencies, from an unnamed western government organisation on 22 July, and also worked UniFi OS, FlowiseAI, Gitea (CVE-2026-60004), Nuclio, SENAITE LIMS, Proxmox VE and PAN-OS GlobalProtect. GreyNoise infers LLM-assisted tooling from how the tool iterated; that is an inference. The GS1900 is a small-office switch. It sits in branch offices, schools, shops and labs, is bought without a security review and is rarely on a patch schedule, which is why a June fix is being exploited in September. Update, 22–24 September: BleepingComputer’s coverage of the GreyNoise research adds no new victims. The federal deadline of 24 September has passed, and four more edge and management flaws joined KEV on 22 September (see the Check Point, F5 and Arista cards). No new development was reported as of 27 September. - CISA KEV catalog; GreyNoise; Zyxel security advisory - Zyxel advisory 16 Jun 2026; KEV-listed and GreyNoise report 21 Sep 2026; BleepingComputer 22 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] Cisco’s firewall-management console has three attack clusters on it — one Sandworm-linked by tooling, one that deployed Qilin — and the hardening advisory, revised on 18 September, is not about exploited flaws
item.description: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center remains the clearest example this month of attackers going after the system that manages the perimeter. CVE-2026-20079 (CVSS 10.0) is an unauthenticated authentication bypass that gives root command execution through crafted HTTP requests; CVE-2026-20316 (CVSS 5.3) is a hardcoded low-privilege credential. Cisco Talos separates the activity into three clusters. UAT-12197, unattributed, uses CVE-2026-20079 to plant JSP web shells and a cmd.jar credential extractor. UAT-11823, which Talos tracks as an APT, chains both flaws and deployed a 64-bit Linux variant of Cyclops Blink, malware previously attributed to Sandworm. Talos says the cluster’s tooling overlaps with Sandworm’s, which makes it Sandworm-linked, not a Sandworm attribution. UAT-11988, assessed with high confidence as a ransomware operator whose tradecraft matches Qilin affiliates, entered through CVE-2026-20316 alone and deployed Qilin on selected endpoints. CISA added CVE-2026-20079 to KEV on 9 September with a 12 September deadline, now passed. Correction: an earlier edition said CVE-2026-20316 had been in KEV since 29 July and was flagged for ransomware use. The KEV catalog has no entry for it; 29 July is when exploitation was first reported. Update, 16 September: Cisco published its September hardening advisory for ASA, FTD and FMC (cisco-sa-hardening-asaftdfmc-uvpPROhN). It covers eight CVEs found in internal review, CVE-2026-20329 to CVE-2026-20336, with fixed FTD and FMC releases 7.0.10, 7.2.12, 7.4.8, 7.6.6, 7.7.13, 10.0.2 and 10.1.0; it went to revision 1.1 on 18 September with an updated ASA fixed-release table. Its statement that two vulnerabilities “belonging to this vulnerability class” are known to be exploited refers to CVE-2026-20079 and CVE-2026-20316, not to the hardening CVEs, which Cisco does not report as exploited. - Cisco PSIRT; Cisco Talos; CISA KEV catalog; BleepingComputer - Talos report 9 Sep 2026; hardening advisory 16 Sep 2026, revised 18 Sep 2026

item.title: [High] CISA added three Linux kernel flaws to KEV with a three-day deadline — nobody has said how they are being exploited, which is a reason to move faster, not slower
item.description: CISA added three Linux kernel vulnerabilities to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 18 September with a federal deadline of 21 September, which has now passed. CVE-2025-39682 is in the kernel TLS receive path, where a zero-length record gets past record-type handling. The Hacker News gives it CVSS 9.8, and Red Hat cites known public exploits. CVE-2026-53266 is an out-of-bounds write in ebtables SNAT handling that leads to privilege escalation, rated CVSS 8.8. CVE-2025-39964 is a race condition in the AF_ALG crypto socket interface, rated CVSS 7.8. Red Hat has updated its advisories to acknowledge exploitation, but nobody has said who is exploiting the flaws, how, or whether they are being used together. As of 22 September that is still the case. Related but distinct: on 18 September a researcher published working local-root exploits for four other kernel flaws, CVE-2026-80844, CVE-2026-81000, CVE-2026-68121 and CVE-2026-74469, fixed in current stable and long-term kernels, according to The Hacker News. Those are proof-of-concept releases, not KEV entries, and do not overlap with the trio; keep the two sets apart when you brief. CISA’s entries carry two notes worth reading closely: affected products may be end-of-life, and the vulnerable component can be embedded in other products. The second note is where most enterprises are exposed. General-purpose servers get kernel updates through the normal distribution channel, but appliances, network devices, hypervisor hosts and container platforms built on Linux often do not. Local privilege escalation also matters most on shared systems. On a container node, a CI runner or a multi-tenant server, anyone who can run code there counts as a local user. - CISA KEV catalog; Red Hat; The Hacker News - KEV-listed 18 Sep 2026; reported 19 Sep 2026; deadline passed 21 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] GitLab’s CVSS 10.0 path traversal reads any file on the server in one unauthenticated request — and went from disclosure to confirmed exploitation in three days
item.description: CVE-2026-85706 is an unauthenticated path traversal in the repository commits interface of self-managed GitLab: a single crafted HTTP request returns the contents of an arbitrary file from the server, with no credentials and no user interaction. GitLab disclosed and patched it on 10–11 September (its patch-release feed dates the release 10 September) in 19.3.2, 19.2.6 and 19.1.8, a release that also fixed CVE-2026-87719, a critical insecure-deserialisation flaw in the Enterprise Edition’s GraphQL subscription handling; no further GitLab patch release had appeared by 22 September. Affected versions run from 18.7 through 19.1.8, 19.2 through 19.2.6 and 19.3 through 19.3.2, and the instance needs at least one public project for the request to land. watchTowr Labs and CISA both reported internet-wide probing almost immediately, and on 14 September CISA and GitLab each confirmed exploitation in the wild; the flaw was added to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 11 September with a federal civilian deadline of 14 September, now passed. On 16 September Hong Kong’s HKCERT also warned that the flaw is being exploited in the wild; no count of compromised instances has been published. GitLab.com SaaS customers were not affected. The reason this is worse than a file-read sounds is what a GitLab server keeps on disk. CI/CD variables, runner registration tokens, deploy keys, integration secrets and database credentials all live there, so an arbitrary read is a credential harvest against every pipeline the instance runs — and those credentials keep working after the patch is applied. - GitLab advisory; CISA KEV catalog; watchTowr Labs; HKCERT; BleepingComputer; Cybersecurity Dive; Dark Reading - Disclosed and patched 10–11 Sep 2026; exploitation confirmed 14 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] A ScreenConnect authorisation flaw is being used to push payloads between connected machines — CISA gave federal agencies three days to patch it
item.description: CVE-2026-84869 is a missing-authorisation and improper-privilege-management flaw in ConnectWise ScreenConnect, rated CVSS 9.9 and confirmed exploited. Attackers abuse legitimate remote-support sessions to transfer and execute files without the host confirming the transfer, then use social engineering to get a victim to run a modified ScreenConnect client that detects active sessions and propagates VBScript payloads to the machines on the other end of them. That is the worm-like behaviour in the reporting: not a self-replicating network worm, but spread along established trust relationships between a support console and the endpoints it already reaches. Exploitation has been reported since 20 August. CISA added the flaw to KEV on 11 September and, under Binding Operational Directive 26-04, gave federal agencies three days to remediate — an unusually compressed clock that is itself a signal about observed activity. ConnectWise fixed it in version 26.6.5, with disabling the TransferFiles permission offered as an interim mitigation. For anyone whose IT is delivered by a managed service provider, the relevant instance may not be one you administer, and the blast radius runs from that provider outward through every client it supports. - ConnectWise advisory; CISA KEV catalog; SecurityWeek - KEV-listed 11 Sep 2026; exploitation reported from 20 Aug 2026

item.title: [Critical] A crafted email is enough to get root on a Cisco Secure Email Gateway — CVE-2026-76461 is under active exploitation and there is no workaround
item.description: Cisco has confirmed active exploitation of CVE-2026-76461, a CVSS 9.8 flaw in Cisco AsyncOS for Secure Email Gateway, physical and virtual, that lets an unauthenticated remote attacker run arbitrary commands with root privileges on the underlying operating system. Reporting describes the path as SQL injection reached through the appliance’s parsing of an inbound message, which is the uncomfortable part: the attack vector is the product doing its job. No user has to click anything, no management interface has to be exposed, and no credential is needed — the gateway accepts hostile input from the internet by design, and that is the input. All configurations are affected and Cisco states there is no workaround; fixes are in AsyncOS 15.5.5-014, 16.0.4-302 and 16.5.0-780, shipped alongside a security-hardening advisory. Cisco revised the advisory to 1.1 on 17 September to add clarification for clustered appliances; the exploitation statement is unchanged, and the advisory’s own indicator is a search of the mail logs for COPY.*TO PROGRAM. Secure Email and Web Manager and Secure Web Appliance are not affected. Cisco says multiple customers were likely compromised before disclosure and has contacted affected Secure Email Cloud customers with indicators of compromise; attribution is unknown. CISA added the flaw to the KEV catalog on 14 September with a federal deadline of 17 September, now passed. Cisco Identity Services Engine has since followed with an exploited CVSS 10.0 zero-day (see above). That makes three Cisco enterprise products on this page under confirmed exploitation, alongside Secure Firewall Management Center, and all three share a shape: perimeter infrastructure that sees everything, trusted implicitly, and rarely covered by endpoint detection. - Cisco PSIRT; CISA KEV catalog; SecurityWeek; The Hacker News; BleepingComputer - Advisory and KEV listing 14 Sep 2026; advisory rev 1.1 17 Sep 2026; FCEB deadline passed 17 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] CISA now marks the VMware vCenter RCE CVE-2026-59310 as used by ransomware — the flaw that was an espionage story in August is now an extortion one
item.description: CISA has updated its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities entry for CVE-2026-59310, a remote code execution flaw in VMware vCenter Server, to record known use in ransomware campaigns, as reported by BleepingComputer on 15 September. Broadcom patched the flaw on 29 July, and CISA added it to the catalog on 18 August with a federal deadline of 21 August. CISA has not named the ransomware groups involved or said how many organisations are affected. The earlier phase of exploitation is better documented: during mid-August APT activity, the DFIR firm QUIRSO counted 361 compromised IP addresses across 47 countries, and Shadowserver has tracked around 450 exposed vCenter servers. The change of status matters more than the change of wording. vCenter is the control plane for a virtualised estate, so an operator with code execution there can reach every guest it manages at once — which is exactly the position an encryption-focused crew wants, and exactly why a host that was quietly compromised in August may now be holding a second, less patient visitor. - CISA KEV catalog; Broadcom; BleepingComputer; QUIRSO; Shadowserver - KEV-listed 18 Aug 2026; ransomware use reported 15 Sep 2026

item.title: [High] Three JFrog Artifactory flaws chain from anonymous token to administrator in under five minutes — and researchers put half of internet-reachable instances still at risk
item.description: Attackers are chaining CVE-2026-42018, a token-disclosure flaw rated CVSS 7.5 that yields an internal anonymous-user JWT even where anonymous access is disabled, with CVE-2026-42016, an insufficient token-validation issue rated CVSS 8.1 that escalates that token to administrator — in some observed cases in under five minutes — before deploying a custom Rust-based command-and-control backdoor. A third flaw, CVE-2026-82329, is a critical authentication bypass in the same product. Attacks were reported publicly from 11 September; Wiz’s timeline puts exploitation of the first two back to 15 August. CISA added those two to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 11 September with a federal deadline of 25 September, now passed, the same day as the four 22 September KEV additions on this page. JFrog has fixed them in 7.111.21 and later, depending on branch. Researchers estimate that between 49% and 62% of internet-reachable Artifactory instances remain vulnerable to at least one of the three. Update, 17 September: Wiz has documented six malicious Groovy user plugins dropped into $JFROG_HOME/var/etc/artifactory/plugins/. They include command shells, a dumper for decrypted LDAP, Crowd and proxy secrets, token tables and signing material, and a memory-resident Tomcat filter backdoor triggered by an X-Request-Trace header. The plugins survive patching and reload on restart, so upgrading closes the way in but leaves the backdoor in place. The severity is not really the CVSS scores, which are moderate individually; it is the position of the product. An artifact registry is the thing your builds trust without checking, so administrator access to it is administrator access to everything compiled, containerised or deployed from it afterwards. - JFrog advisory; CISA KEV catalog; Wiz; BleepingComputer; SecurityWeek - Attacks reported 11 Sep 2026; KEV-listed 11 Sep 2026; Wiz persistence update 17 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] Google patched the seventh Chrome zero-day of 2026 — and four separate espionage groups were already running the same exploit kit that uses it
item.description: Google released a Chrome update on 9 September fixing CVE-2026-87491, an out-of-bounds write in V8, the browser’s JavaScript and WebAssembly engine, and confirmed the flaw is being exploited in the wild. A crafted HTML page is enough to execute code inside the renderer sandbox. The fixed builds are 153.0.8010.36 and .37. This is the seventh actively exploited Chrome zero-day Google has patched in 2026, and it arrives five days after the sixth, CVE-2026-85046, which is also still worth confirming across your fleet. What makes it more than a routine browser patch is who was already using it: researchers found four distinct nation-state-linked groups, one of them APT31 from 28 August, running the same exploit kit — tracked as BlueMoon — chaining CVE-2026-85046 and CVE-2026-87491 inside a single week. Four unrelated actors converging on one chain that fast points at a shared exploit broker rather than four independent discoveries. Two practical notes decide whether you are actually protected. Chrome applies its update on restart, so a fleet where nobody closes the browser is a fleet that is not patched. And every Chromium-based browser in the estate inherits this: Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi and any embedded Electron application ship their own V8 and need their own updates on their own vendor schedules. Update: CISA added CVE-2026-87491 to the KEV catalog on 9 September with a federal deadline of 23 September, now passed. Google has since shipped Chrome 153.0.8010.52 and .53 on 17 September with 16 further fixes, two of them rated Critical (CVE-2026-93374 in the Dawn graphics layer and CVE-2026-93372 in WebGL), with no in-the-wild statement for any of them, so the current build is the target rather than .36. - Google Chrome release blog; CISA KEV catalog; The Hacker News - Patched and KEV-listed 9 Sep 2026; BlueMoon research 9 Sep 2026; Chrome 153.0.8010.52/.53 on 17 Sep 2026

item.title: [Info] CIRCIA’s final incident-reporting rule is at White House review and still unpublished — anything quoted as “the rule” today is the 2024 proposal
item.description: The final rule under the Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act (CIRCIA) has gone to the White House Office of Management and Budget for review, BankInfoSecurity reported on 2 October, and it had not appeared in the Federal Register as of 6 October. The federal regulatory agenda had targeted September 2026; the October 2025 statutory deadline and a May 2026 target were also missed. The final text is not public. The figures in circulation, 72 hours to report a covered cyber incident and 24 hours to report a ransom payment, come from the 2024 proposed rule and could change. Infosecurity Magazine quotes an expert who expects the duties to start in late 2026 or 2027. GAO’s 28 September report on overlapping reporting rules (see that card) shows why the final terms matter. - BankInfoSecurity; Federal Register (Unified Agenda); Infosecurity Magazine; HIPAA Journal - Sent for OMB review (reported 2 Oct 2026); not published as of 6 Oct 2026

item.title: [Info] GAO’s industry panel says overlapping federal cyber-reporting rules make it hard to report and respond at the same time — DHS and SEC rules are seen as duplicating sector rules
item.description: The US Government Accountability Office published GAO-26-109197 on 28 September, drawing on a virtual panel held on 16 July with six industry representatives from energy, financial services and healthcare. Panellists said it could be difficult to fully satisfy all reporting requirements while remediating cyber threats, saw DHS and SEC rules as duplicating sector-specific ones, and half agreed that progress on harmonisation had been limited. They suggested consistent timeframes, thresholds and definitions, a lead agency such as CISA to coordinate reporting, and more collaboration between government and industry. The report makes no formal recommendations. National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross separately pledged on 29 September to harmonise the reporting structure. - GAO; Cybersecurity Dive; Industrial Cyber - Panel 16 Jul 2026; published 28 Sep 2026

item.title: [Low] A Europol-supported operation takes down the KillSec ransomware group’s leak site and arrests three people, including a teenager suspected of leading the group
item.description: Europol announced on 30 September an operation against the KillSec ransomware group: three arrests and eight searches in four European countries, the group’s leak site seized and more than 110 TB of stolen data secured. Europol says the suspected leader is a teenager. Outlets give differing counts of the group’s claimed victims, so this card does not state one. item.title: [Low] CISA and NIST set concrete numbers for cloud identity tokens and signing keys — one-hour tokens, 90-day key rotation for high-impact systems, and no tokens in logs
item.description: CISA and NIST have co-authored NIST IR 8587, guidance on protecting the identity tokens and signing keys that cloud authentication depends on. The recommendations are specific. Access and identity tokens should be valid for at most one hour, and expired tokens should be rejected outright. Signing keys should be rotated every 90 days for high-impact systems and annually for others. They should be kept in hardware-backed or isolated storage, and high-impact systems should do their signing in isolated environments. The audience claim should be mandatory, and tokens should never be written to logs. The report cites the 2020 SAML-forgery supply-chain attack, and the incident in which forged tokens exposed more than 60,000 government emails, as the failures it is designed to prevent. It is voluntary and aimed at federal agencies, cloud providers and cloud buyers, which makes it most useful as a procurement and architecture checklist. It landed in a week when the Brevo incident turned on a long-lived, over-privileged API key stored in source code, and identity infrastructure such as Cisco ISE was under attack. Long lifetimes, keys that never rotate and tokens left in logs are common, and each is easy to measure. - CISA; NIST; Infosecurity Magazine - Published 15 Sep 2026
